title: Central Clearing Implementation (TBAC Charge 1, Q2 2026)
date_evidence: Central Clearing Implementation May 2026 ... Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee Quarterly Meeting Committee Charge – May 5, 2026
key_claim: Cash Treasury activity potentially subject to clearing averaged approximately $550 billion in daily ATS plus interdealer volume in 2025, up approximately 20% from 2024; FICC sponsored DVP and GC repo volumes rose over 150% in two years, from $1.113 trillion at end-2023 to $2.856 trillion on 30 December 2025; OFR estimates approximately 58% of repo volumes subject to the clearing mandate are already being cleared; an August 2025 pulse survey of 330 industry experts found 47% of firms very confident and 41% somewhat confident of meeting deadlines, 88% saying they cannot finalise preparation without more operating-model clarity, fewer than one in three firms very familiar with done-away clearing, and operational readiness and re-papering cited as the biggest worries by up to 71% of firms; done-away outstanding items include a lack of standardized documentation, uncertainty around the pre-trade credit check sequencing, required operational builds and commercial clarity on pricing; bespoke done-with agreements can take months to years to negotiate; the committee concludes it is possible that clearing will not be available to all participants in all regions by the deadline.
frame_summary: TBAC argues that despite steady industry progress and strong voluntary volume growth, unresolved inter-affiliate and extraterritorial scoping, immature done-away market structure and heavy documentation burdens mean the official sector must deliver near-term clarity or accept that clearing will not be available to all participants in all regions by the deadlines.
notes: Anchor for the readiness-gap and done-away strands. Presented at the 5 May 2026 TBAC meeting; title page reads May 2026; companion minutes published 6 May 2026.

title: Minutes of the Meeting of the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee, May 5, 2026
date_evidence: Minutes of the Meeting of the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee May 5, 2026 — May 6, 2026 (press-release dateline); meta-og:updated_time: 2026-05-06
key_claim: The TBAC presenter reviewed progress by industry and regulators, highlighted the recent inter-affiliate and extraterritorial exemption requests as key outstanding issues to resolve, and concluded that although the industry has made steady progress, some operational and implementation challenges remain as the market transitions to expanded central clearing; dealers also viewed the modified eSLR and March 2026 bank capital proposals as helpful to Treasury market intermediation.
frame_summary: Treasury's advisory committee frames expanded central clearing as important for Treasury market functioning but records that unresolved exemption requests and operational challenges are the live risks to a smooth transition.
notes: Official minutes of the meeting at which the Central Clearing Implementation charge was presented.

title: Update on the SEC's Work Toward Treasury Clearing Implementation (Commissioner Mark T. Uyeda)
date_evidence: Washington D.C. April 20, 2026 ... Last Reviewed or Updated: April 20, 2026
key_claim: The SEC published for comment SIFMA's request to modify the inter-affiliate exemption and reopened the comment period on IIB's request on the extraterritorial application of the trade submission requirement; the US Treasury market is nearly $29 trillion outstanding; compliance dates are 31 December 2026 for cash and 30 June 2027 for repo; the Commission has approved new clearing agencies (CME Securities Clearing, December 2025; ICE Clear Credit, January 2026) and FICC access-model changes; staff continue to assess failed trades, clearing agency outages and customer protection, issues market participants have repeatedly identified as critical to their preparations.
frame_summary: The SEC's lead commissioner on implementation argues the mandate is progressing methodically and will not be delayed again, while conceding that scope-defining exemption requests and failed-trade, outage and customer-protection questions remain unresolved close to the deadline.
notes: Names the two exemption requests as intersecting scope decisions; comment deadline on both was 29 May 2026.

title: SEC Approves Exemptive Order and Proposed Rule Change to Permit Customer Cross-Margining in the U.S. Treasury Market
date_evidence: For Immediate Release 2026-36 Washington D.C., April 15, 2026
key_claim: The SEC issued a conditional exemptive order permitting customer cross-margining of cash Treasury positions cleared at a registered clearing agency and Treasury futures cleared at a derivatives clearing organization, and approved FICC's Third Amended and Restated Cross-Margining Agreement with CME; prior to the order only clearing members could cross-margin such positions.
frame_summary: The SEC presents customer cross-margining as a completed implementation step that unlocks liquidity and capital efficiency and keeps the Treasury market resilient through the clearing transition.
notes: Extends the FICC-CME cross-margining arrangement from house accounts to customer positions.

title: How the U.S. Treasury Futures Market and the Basis Trade Could Be Affected by the Treasury Clearing Mandate: Part 2 - The Possible Role of Cross-Margining (Chicago Fed Letter No. 517)
key_claim: As of 2023 only 35% of Treasury repo trades were centrally cleared, a share expected to rise to 84% under the mandate; for a hedged ten-year cash-futures basis trade, required collateral without cross-margining would be around $20 million, double the $10 million required today, while with cross-margining it could be around 75% less than the no-cross-margining scenario and below current levels; leveraged funds constitute about 40% of the Treasury futures market, so absent cross-margining the mandate could deter basis trading and reduce liquidity in both Treasury futures and securities markets.
frame_summary: The Chicago Fed author argues the mandate's effect on Treasury market liquidity hinges on whether CCP cross-margining is extended to clients: without it collateral costs roughly double and participation falls, with it cleared basis trading could become cheaper than today.
notes: Structural anchor: canonical quantified framing of the margin economics the mandate imposes. Published January 2026, inside the 3-6 month anchor band.

title: Request for Exemptive Relief from the Clearing Rule for Certain Inter-Affiliate Transactions
key_claim: SIFMA requests Section 36 exemptive relief to make the inter-affiliate exemption available to any GAAP-consolidated affiliate of a direct participant except investment company entities, arguing that restrictions on the current exemption, in particular the outward-facing condition and the limited set of covered affiliates, effectively negate its utility for internal treasury, liquidity and collateral management.
frame_summary: The dealer industry body argues the clearing rule's inter-affiliate exemption is unusable as written and that without relief firms' internal liquidity and collateral flows will be forced into clearing at substantial cost with no systemic-risk benefit.
notes: Industry association position letter; the request the SEC published for comment on 17 April 2026.

title: CME-FICC Cross-Margin Program
date_evidence: Evergreen programme page, no publication date; page states the program 'will be expanded to customer accounts beginning April 30, 2026' and cites margin savings of up to 80%.
key_claim: The CME-FICC cross-margin program allows participants to achieve margin savings and capital efficiencies of up to 80% for eligible positions held with a common clearing member, has generated margin reductions that exceed $1 billion per day for its users, and is being expanded to customer accounts beginning 30 April 2026 ahead of the SEC clearing mandates.
frame_summary: CME markets cross-margining as the capital-efficiency answer to the clearing mandate, positioning its partnership with FICC as the route by which cleared Treasury trading becomes cheaper rather than dearer.
notes: Vendor page used only as directional corroboration of cross-margining economics; savings figures are CME's own.
